clue.text: Lapse morally, kicking out Labour's leader, the arse!

indicators.note: a party's leader stands at the front, so the opening letter of the word is taken
kicking someone out removes them, so a letter is dropped from the word for lapsing

blocks.note: to backslide is to relapse into bad ways
the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A rant at a politician who has strayed morally and sacked the party leader, branding him an arse.
explanation.walkthrough: BACKSLIDE loses its L to give BACKSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal names for the buttocks, the part a person sits on.

clue.text: (& 23dn.) "Queer", "butch" am I? That's uncalled-for

indicators.note: queer means odd or out of true, so the letters that follow are set in a strange new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone bristles at being labelled, protesting that the questions about their sexuality are out of line.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 2 and 23 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark that goes too far, excessive or unwarranted, is said to be over the top; the phrase means exactly that.

clue.text: Aroused or just expectant?

blocks.note: first meaning: woken by a knock at the door, an old British usage
second meaning: slang for made pregnant

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a lodger could ask to be roused by a knock in the morning; 'Aroused' looks sexual but means woken.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is old British for woken by knocking, and vulgar slang for pregnant, an expectant mother.

clue.text: Resolved to get female cousin playing around

indicators.note: playing around suggests messing about, so the letters are moved out of their order

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for female
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has made up their mind about a cousin who is sleeping around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' reads as decided, but here it is the optical sense of a sharp image.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens has resolved an image when the picture is sharp and clear, with detail properly distinguished.

clue.text: Being before court is hard

blocks.note: ere is an old word for before
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Appearing before a judge is a tough ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff and standing up, as a penis when aroused, which is the cheeky sense the setter intends here.

clue.text: Woman squeezing organ-like appendage – a source of caviare

indicators.note: to squeeze something is to hold it tightly within, so the woman's name wraps around the next part

blocks.note: a short form of the woman's name Beatrice
lug is slang for an ear, an organ that sticks out

explanation.surface: A woman clutching something shaped like a body part, oddly linked to fish roe.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga sturgeon of the Caspian yields the most prized and expensive caviar.

clue.text: Biographer makes Blair's head get inflated – nothing inside it, though!

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the name is used
being inside means being placed within the letters around it

blocks.note: the first letter of Blair
zero, written as the letter O
to swell is to grow bigger, as if blown up

explanation.surface: A jibe that Tony Blair's head has swollen with pride though there is nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The O for nothing goes into B plus SWELL, just after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell wrote the celebrated Life of Samuel Johnson, a classic of English biography.

clue.text: One who sponges dirty old man holding very end of sponge

indicators.note: the very end of a word is its final letter alone
holding means keeping something within, so the old man wraps round the letter

blocks.note: a lech is a lecherous man
the last letter of sponge

explanation.surface: A sleazy old man clutching a bath sponge is himself a freeloader.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a parasite who lives off others, just as a sponger cadges without giving back.

clue.text: Olive might bugger off!

blocks.note: first meaning: an olive can be filled with pimento or similar
second meaning: a rude British dismissal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Olive' looks like a woman's name telling someone to go away; it is the fruit, which can be filled.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffed olives are filled with pimento; the phrase is also a crude British way of telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Hack, rotten fraud

blocks.note: to hack or tear something apart
food gone bad is off

explanation.surface: A journalist dismissed as a rotten fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' suggests a journalist, a Private Eye favourite, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle or overpriced deal that cheats the customer is a common informal term for a con.

clue.text: Measures taken by old PM to put on a condom?

blocks.note: ens are printers' units of width
Edward Heath, British Prime Minister 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: Steps a former Prime Minister might take to practise safe sex.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as a playful example: putting on a condom is one way of covering something in a sheath.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensheath is to enclose in a covering; a condom is literally called a sheath in Britain.

clue.text: (& 22dn.) Really beat? Come off heroin and reveal sexual nature, old fellow!

blocks.note: to kick a habit is to give it up, and shit is slang for heroin
to out someone is to reveal they are gay
O for old and F for fellow

explanation.surface: Advice to someone shattered: quit drugs, come out of the closet, old chap!
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 11 across and 22 down.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a violent thrashing is to batter them thoroughly, a coarse idiom for a severe beating.

clue.text: A real oldie, Cyclops, so piss up comes before hospital

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the setter is Cyclops, so the setter refers to himself
so and thus both mean therefore
piss is slang for weak beer
H is the map symbol for a hospital

explanation.surface: The setter, an old soak, admits that getting drunk comes before ending up in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Methuselah is the biblical patriarch said to have lived 969 years, a byword for great age.

clue.text: Brenda's gobbled by new heartthrob, a bit like Mr Bean?

indicators.note: being gobbled means being swallowed, so the name is taken inside the other letters

blocks.note: Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina
N is the abbreviation for new
a dish is an attractive person

explanation.surface: The Queen being devoured by a dishy young man, the sort of farce Mr Bean might star in.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen. Mr Bean is Rowan Atkinson's gawky, socially inept comic character.
explanation.definitionFit: Being socially awkward and unfashionable, as Rowan Atkinson's comic character is, means having the traits of a geek.

clue.text: Curse of western women: getting back with Dicky

indicators.note: getting back means going backwards, so the word is written in reverse

blocks.note: gals is the Western, American cowboy word for women
dicky is British slang for unwell or faulty, as is off

explanation.surface: The bane of cowgirls is going back to an unreliable man called Dicky.
explanation.walkthrough: To slag off is British slang for to insult or criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbally abusing someone is cursing them; the British phrase means to rubbish or insult a person.

clue.text: Bush starts to initiate illegal invasions – a ruler presiding over the dispossession of America

definitions.text: a ruler presiding over the dispossession of America

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the first of each is kept

blocks.note: George Bush, US President
the opening letters of three words

explanation.surface: A complaint that George W Bush starts illegal wars, set beside the king who lost America.
explanation.definitionFit: King George III was on the British throne when the thirteen American colonies won independence.

clue.text: Bicycle tool

blocks.note: first meaning: the Raleigh ..., a famous 1970s British bike
second meaning: an axe for chopping, and slang for a penis

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tool' is doubly loaded: a chopping axe, and the vulgar slang both words share.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raleigh Chopper was a high-handlebarred kids' bike; a cleaver or axe is also so named, as is a penis.

clue.text: Curtailed mega-bore, pisspoor Boycott

indicators.note: to curtail is literally to cut off the tail, so the last letter goes
something pisspoor is badly made, so the letters are put together in a new way

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A dreadful bore is cut short and shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott, the Yorkshire cricketer, is lurking in the surface as the mega-bore.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban on trade, a formal shunning of a country or goods.

clue.text: Hack's dream: Brenda's shit collector?

blocks.note: every journalist longs for an exclusive story
Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A tabloid fantasy that the Queen collects dog mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a pooper-scooper picks up dog mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A pooper-scooper is a tool for picking up dog droppings, so it gathers excrement.

clue.text: Saint takes crown – "I do an Alistair Campbell!"

blocks.note: CR is the abbreviation for crown
taken as written
Alastair Campbell was Tony Blair's spin doctor

explanation.surface: A holy man seizes power and boasts of putting his own gloss on events like Blair's press chief.
explanation.definitionFit: St Crispin, patron of shoemakers, is remembered for St Crispin's Day, the date of Agincourt.

clue.text: Fellatio with a condom? Criminal activity!

blocks.note: first meaning: protected oral sex, read as a jokey phrase
second meaning: cracking a strongbox with explosives

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical literal reading, flagged by the question mark; the second is the real dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking into strongboxes by blasting them open is a burglar's trade; read literally the words suggest protected oral sex.

clue.text: Aspect of Cherie: extremely thick all round

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two outermost letters
all round means surrounding, so one part encloses the other

blocks.note: thick and fat both mean stout or broad
the first and last letters of Cherie

explanation.surface: A dig that Cherie Blair is stupid through and through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick' reads as stupid but supplies a word for stout.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one side or feature of something, as an aspect is one part of a situation.

clue.text: (see 11ac.)
(see 2dn.)
Conrad: an arse and a pest

blocks.note: Conrad Black, the newspaper proprietor later jailed for fraud
a rat is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: An attack on the press baron Conrad Black as a nasty piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: The black rat is the species of rodent that spread plague, a classic household vermin.

clue.text: Like committed members needing power to help to get erect

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power
aid and help are synonyms
standing upright

explanation.surface: Smutty talk of members needing assistance to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' plays on the slang sense of penis; here it means members of a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Members who have paid their subscriptions are fully signed up and so loyal, devoted adherents of the club or party.

clue.text: Got the shakes? Group outside

indicators.note: something with the shakes trembles about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone is trembling with nerves as a gang waits outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is an area where a minority lives segregated, set apart from mainstream society as outsiders.

clue.text: Sun insinuates itself into hallway via this nut, Ray?

definitions.text: Sun insinuates itself into hallway via this

blocks.note: a nut is an enthusiast
a ray is a beam

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about sunlight creeping into a hall and an odd man called Ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' hints at the tabloid newspaper, but it is the sunshine itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanlight is the semicircular window above a front door that lets daylight into an entrance hall.
